summary: Read the full parsed text (pages 1–18, including abstract, body, tables, footnotes and appendices). The prose is generally clean. Five isolated copyediting issues were found: a subject–verb disagreement, an unfilled placeholder, a broken parallel construction, and two missing commas. Quotes for findings on pages 6 and 10 were confirmed against the rendered page images.

findings.finding_summary: Subject–verb disagreement in footnote 3: "The 96 articles consists of".
findings.claim_text: The 96 articles consists of the 92 articles from rounds 2–4 (Section 5) and four from the pilot run.
findings.evidence_summary: The plural subject "The 96 articles" takes a singular verb in footnote 3. Confirmed in the rendered page 10 image (footnote at the bottom of the page).

source_objects.label: Page 10 rendered image
source_objects.verification_note: Inspected the page 10 image, footnote 3 at the bottom of the page. It reads "The 96 articles consists of the 92 articles from rounds 2–4 (Section 5) and four from the pilot run." The same wording appears in parsed pages/page_010.md.

claim_evidence_links.claim_text: The 96 articles consists of the 92 articles from rounds 2–4

findings.suggested_fix: Change "consists" to "consist": "The 96 articles consist of the 92 articles from rounds 2–4 (Section 5) and four from the pilot run."

findings.finding_summary: The title-page author contribution for Valentin Bayas is an unfilled placeholder, "[add contribution]".
findings.evidence_summary: Every other author has a contribution statement. This entry still contains drafting placeholder text.

claim_evidence_links.note: Placeholder text left in the manuscript.

findings.suggested_fix: Replace the placeholder with the actual contribution statement.

findings.finding_summary: Broken parallel structure in coding rule 3: "are linked ... and counted as metadata" leaves the subject of "counted" unclear.

location.text_quote: as with the four articles about Homborsund and counted as metadata to analyse coverage

findings.claim_text: Articles about the same project are linked to a single project record, as with the four articles about Homborsund and counted as metadata to analyse coverage.
findings.evidence_summary: "counted as metadata" attaches grammatically to "the four articles about Homborsund", and the intended parallel with "are linked" is lost. The reader must infer the intended meaning. Confirmed in the rendered page 6 image, item 3 of the list; the sentence wraps across lines there.

source_objects.label: Page 6 rendered image
source_objects.verification_note: Inspected the page 6 image, item 3 "One record per event" at the top of the page. It reads "...linked to a single project record, as with the four articles about Homborsund and counted as metadata to analyse coverage." The quote wraps across three lines in the rendering, so the block-level JSON text did not match as a single string.

claim_evidence_links.claim_text: Articles about the same project are linked to a single project record ... and counted as metadata to analyse coverage.
claim_evidence_links.note: Sentence structure obscures what is counted as metadata.

findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite, for example: "Articles about the same project are linked to a single project record, as with the four articles about Homborsund, and the number of articles per project is recorded as metadata to analyse coverage."

findings.finding_summary: Missing comma before "for example" at the end of the sentence.

location.section: 6.1 An application to house listing data
location.text_quote: short cycling distance to the city centre for example

findings.claim_text: real estate agents may instead have described a short cycling distance to the city centre for example.
findings.evidence_summary: The sentence-final "for example" needs to be set off with a comma. In the rendered page 10 image the phrase wraps from "city centre" to "for example." on the next line, with no comma.

source_objects.label: Page 10 rendered image
source_objects.verification_note: Inspected the page 10 image, the third paragraph of Section 6.1 ("As a first step, Appendix A ..."). It reads "...as real estate agents may instead have described a short cycling distance to the city centre for example." The phrase wraps across two lines, which is why the block-level text did not match as a single string.

claim_evidence_links.claim_text: a short cycling distance to the city centre for example

findings.finding_summary: Missing comma before "but" joining two independent clauses.

location.text_quote: cycling paths in this pilot but the analysis could easily be expanded

findings.claim_text: We restrict the search to articles discussing cycling paths in this pilot but the analysis could easily be expanded to include other types of bicycle or transport infrastructure.
findings.evidence_summary: Two independent clauses are joined by "but" with no comma, which makes the long sentence harder to read.

source_objects.text_quote: cycling paths in this pilot but the analysis could easily be expanded

claim_evidence_links.claim_text: We restrict the search ... in this pilot but the analysis could easily be expanded

findings.suggested_fix: Insert a comma: "...in this pilot, but the analysis could easily be expanded..."

notes: Scope was limited to grammar and copyediting. Content, numbers, references and citations were not assessed.
Footnote markers attached to words in the extraction (for example "projects3") were treated as parser artifacts and not reported.

evidence_limitations: Review relied mainly on text extraction. Only pages 6 and 10 were inspected as rendered images, so typographic issues visible only in the rendered PDF on other pages would not be detected.

coverage.check_performed: Read the whole parsed full text and audited it for grammar, typos, duplicated words, punctuation and sentence clarity. Quotes on pages 6 and 10 were verified against the rendered page images; the other quotes were verified against the registered page block text.
coverage.reason: Exhaustive read of the manuscript text. Five low- or medium-severity copyedit findings were recorded. Parser artifacts such as footnote markers attached to words were deliberately not reported.
